AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 17, 2021
UUNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL
MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION.
TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING, ATTEND THE MEETING IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS,
SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING:
(669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685 DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK
ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON
THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  4:30 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a)
  – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County Sheriff representative, and other related City
  officials.

  II.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54957: Various positions.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  April Reutter
  Pray Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Julio De La Hoya
  Youth Commissioner/Summer Youth Worker

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize the 2021 Home & Business Beautification Contest Winners.

  II.  City Council to recognize the Finance Department for obtaining the Government Finance Officers
  Association Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  National Night Out recap.

  3.  United States Navy TAOC Los Angeles Ribbon Cutting.
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of August
  3, 2021. 825-04

  Report

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period July 11, 2021 – July 24,
  2021, in the total amount of $937,595.15. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period July
  29, 2021 – August 11, 2021, in the total amount of $10,021,462.36. 640

  Report

  5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Manuel L.
  Mora, Adriana Serrano, and George Zaragoza. 830-13/19/26

  Report

  6.  ORDINANCE NO. 21-1727 – GRANTING A PIPELINE FRANCHISE TO TORRANCE PIPELINE
  COMPANY, LLC. - Staff recommends City Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  21-1727, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK GRANTING A PIPELINE FRANCHISE TO
  TORRANCE PIPELIINE COMPANY, LLC. 618-03

  Report

  7.  PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT WITH NORWALK-LA MIRADA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT
  TO PROVIDE COMPRESSED NATURAL GAS FUEL - Staff recommends City Council approve a
  Purchase and Sale Agreement with Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District for a period of three (3)
  years, from September 18, 2021 – September 18, 2024, to allow the District to fuel buses at the City’s
  Compressed Natural Gas station; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 530-04/920-10-02

  Report

  8.  ACCEPT WORK FOR CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS AUDIO/VIDEO UPGRADE PROJECT - Staff
  recommends City Council accept the work of EIDIM of Buena Park, for upgrade of the City Hall Council
  Chambers audio/video system, in the amount of $138,110.74. 920-01-04

  Report

  9.  RESOLUTION NO 21–52 - BUDGET AMENDMENT ACCEPTING STATE FUNDS TO SUPPORT THE
  VETERANS AFFORDABLE HOUSING PROJECT NO. 7847 IN THE AMOUNT OF $3,000,000 - Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 21–52, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK, AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22
  ADOPTED BUDGET TO ACCEPT STATE FUNDS TO SUPPORT THE VETERANS AFFORDABLE
  HOUSING PROJECT NO. 7847 IN THE AMOUNT OF $3,000,000 AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY
  MANAGER TO EXECUTE ANY DOCUMENTS IN CONNECTION WITH THE PROJECT’S FUNDING.
  610/1005-04-7847

  Report

  10. APPROVAL OF THE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT PROPOSED FUNDING ALLOCATIONS – Staff
   recommends City Council approve the American Rescue Plan Act $28 million Allocation Plan. 622-01

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200 RESOLUTION

  Report

  12. PROJECT NO. 3302-2122 - RESOLUTION NO. 21-51 – BUDGET AMENDMENT AND AWARD OF
  CONTRACT FOR ANNUAL CITYWIDE SIDEWALK CONCRETE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT,
  ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 21-16 – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-51, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE MEASURE R BOND FUNDS AND APPROPRIATE
  TRANSPORTATION DEVELOPMENT ACT ARTICLE 3 FUNDS FOR AMERICANS WITH
  DISABILITIES ACT CURB RAMP INSTALLATIONS TO PROJECT NO. 3302-2122 - ANNUAL
  CITYWIDE SIDEWALK CONCRETE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT, in the amount of $86,155;
  and

  b.  award a contract to Towo Enterprise, Inc. of Corona in the amount of $351,050 for Project No.
  3302-2122, citywide sidewalk concrete repair and replacement; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement and any extension/amendments including potential change orders,
  provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney. 610/1005-04-3302

  Report

REPORTS

  13. DONATION OF SURPLUSED VEHICLES TO HEARTLAND COALITION - THE 501(C) NON-PROFIT
  ORGANIZATION - Staff recommends City Council approve donating surplused vehicles listed in
  Attachment No. 2 to Heartland Coalition.

  Report

  14. SECOND HOMELESS OPERATION PREVENTION AND ENGAGEMENT TEAM ASSESSMENT –
  Staff recommends City Council receive and file.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated August 13, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
